result:
No actions this turn. The skill requires one more step before the write-up: they pick how it gets built, in a message of its own.

---

Thanks, the what is settled. One choice remains before I write it up: how to build it. We haven't talked about that yet, and it shapes the whole design.

Both options use what you already have: Flask, SQLite and the one Pi in the office. Both use a USB barcode scanner that acts as a keyboard. It "types" the lot number into a field, so it needs no drivers and suits wet hands.

1. **Add batch tracking to the taproom app.** You get new pages and new tables in the same database. It is one app to run, update and back up, so this is the least work. The cost is that a bad taproom update could also take down brew-day records.

2. **Build a separate small app on the same Pi.** It gets its own database. Taproom changes can never touch your trace records, which matters if you ever need to answer a recall. The cost is two apps to start, update and back up.

I recommend option 1. The Pi already runs one app well, and you already back it up. I will design the batch tables as their own block, so you could split them out later without a rewrite.

This is a project, not a small change. I will write a full design in `specs/`. A reviewer will read it first, and I may come back once with a few short questions. The folder is not a git repository yet, so I will run `git init` to commit the design, unless you object.

Do you want option 1, or do you want the trace records kept apart in their own app?
